Data Storage & External Services

Catalog items, brands, and types are stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework; the plain .NET configuration uses LocalDB while the Compose configuration points to a SQL Server container. Image storage can use Azure Blob Storage or the local mock implementation. Azure Active Directory is an optional OpenID Connect provider, and Application Insights receives telemetry.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC application separates controllers from catalog and image services, with Autofac managing their lifetimes.
  • Catalog persistence uses an Entity Framework context; mock-data mode substitutes an in-memory catalog service.
  • Authentication and Azure image storage are selected through configuration flags.

DTOs & Contracts

There are no dedicated API DTOs. CatalogItem is the MVC form/model type, and PaginatedItemsViewModel is used for catalog listing data. CatalogBrand and CatalogType are related domain types. The image upload response is an anonymous JSON object containing a name and URL. These classes are mutable; no OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contracts were found. MVC/Razor handles page rendering, and the upload action uses MVC JSON serialization.

Communication Patterns

Controllers call application services directly and synchronously. CatalogService uses Entity Framework to communicate with SQL Server. ImageAzureStorage uses the Azure Storage SDK for Blob operations. No queues, event bus, service discovery, gateway aggregation, retry policy, circuit breaker, or client-side load balancing were found.

When UseAzureActiveDirectory is enabled, OWIN uses cookie and OpenID Connect middleware. Otherwise, a custom middleware creates a placeholder identity. Catalog mutation actions require Authorize; the image-upload action is not explicitly protected. The Compose mapping exposes the application over HTTP; TLS termination is not defined in the project Compose files.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. Docker Compose starts sql.data before eshop.modernized.mvc through depends_on.
  2. The SQL service has a Compose health check in the override file, but the application dependency does not wait on a health condition.
  3. If mock data is disabled, application startup configures the EF initializer, seeds catalog records, and creates SQL sequences.
  4. Application startup initializes image storage and telemetry. Azure services are required only when their corresponding features are enabled.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining an online product catalog, including item descriptions, prices, stock thresholds, brands, types, and pictures. It does not implement shopping-cart, checkout, or order-processing workflows in this solution.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemeShopModernizedMVC / CatalogProduct entry displayed and maintained by the catalogBelongs to one brand and one type
CatalogBrandeShopModernizedMVC / CatalogBrand classification for productsCan be associated with multiple catalog items
CatalogTypeeShopModernizedMVC / CatalogType classification for productsCan be associated with multiple catalog items
Catalog pictureImage service / Catalog mediaImage associated with a productReferenced by the catalog item; image bytes are stored separately

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server through Entity Framework
ImageAzureStorageCatalog mediaCatalog picture blobsAzure Blob Storage
CatalogServiceMockCatalog (mock mode)In-memory catalog itemsNone

All domain operations are within one application. Image operations are delegated to the configured image service; there are no cross-service domain APIs or event exchanges.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog listing or a product details page.
  2. CatalogController requests paginated items or one item from ICatalogService.
  3. The service reads item, brand, and type information from the database, or from the in-memory mock catalog.
  4. The controller builds picture URLs and returns a server-rendered view.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. An authorized user opens the create or edit form and selects catalog type and brand options.
  2. The user can upload an image; PicController accepts the supported image formats and returns a temporary image URL.
  3. The user submits the item form. MVC model validation checks the submitted model; invalid input returns the form with validation errors.
  4. For a valid submission, ICatalogService creates or updates the catalog record. If a temporary image was selected, the configured image service updates the stored picture.
  5. The application redirects to the catalog listing.

Workflow 3: Delete a catalog item

  1. An authorized user views the delete confirmation page.
  2. The user confirms deletion.
  3. CatalogController retrieves the catalog item and asks ICatalogService to remove it from the database or mock collection.
  4. The application redirects to the catalog listing.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is no service-to-service composition. Catalog item data is read from the single relational data store. When Azure image storage is enabled, the application stores image blobs separately and places the resulting image reference in the catalog record. If mock mode is enabled, the mock image service returns local image paths instead.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Catalog editor" participant Pic as "PicController" participant Image as "Image service" participant Catalog as "CatalogController" participant Service as "CatalogService" participant DB as "SQL Server" User->>Pic: Upload product image Pic->>Pic: Validate image format alt Supported image Pic->>Image: Store temporary image Image-->>Pic: Temporary image URL Pic-->>User: Image name and URL User->>Catalog: Submit catalog item Catalog->>Catalog: Validate submitted model alt Model is valid Catalog->>Service: Create or update item Service->>DB: Persist catalog data DB-->>Service: Save result Service-->>Catalog: Completion Catalog->>Image: Update stored image Image-->>Catalog: Image update result Catalog-->>User: Redirect to catalog listing else Model is invalid Catalog-->>User: Return form with validation errors end else Unsupported image Pic-->>User: Bad request end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item name is required. Price must be nonnegative, at most 1,000,000, and have no more than two decimal places.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock threshold must each be between 0 and 10,000,000.
  • Items are associated with an existing brand and type. No rule enforcing relationships among the three stock values was identified.
  • Catalog mutations are guarded by MVC Authorize attributes. Browse and image-upload actions do not have the same explicit attribute.
  • Catalog identifiers are generated from SQL sequences in database mode and from the current maximum item identifier in mock mode.
  • Startup seeding chooses built-in data or optional CSV customization data. No order lifecycle, payment, approval, or background workflow was identified.
  • Persistence is performed synchronously through Entity Framework; no distributed transaction or saga is present.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses ASP.NET MVC 5 and Entity Framework 6, so modernization involves a legacy web stack rather than a current .NET platform. Several Azure libraries and supporting packages are older versions. The NuGet CLI dependency listing could not load Visual Studio WebApplication targets in this environment, so this inventory uses the resolved package entries in packages.config.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config contains 146 package entries, including many System.* and Microsoft.Extensions support packages.
  • Microsoft.Net.Compilers is marked as a development dependency, but no test framework packages or test project were found in this solution.
  • Azure Key Vault, managed identity, Blob Storage, and Application Insights integrations are configured as optional application capabilities.
  • GitHub Advisory checks for the 146 package entries returned no matching advisories; this does not establish that packages are current or risk-free.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The data model consists of three catalog entities stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework 6. A separate image service can store picture content in Azure Blob Storage; the application also supports mock data and image implementations.

Catalog data is seeded at initialization from built-in data or optional CSV files. SQL sequence scripts support identifier generation. No EF migration history or external schema migration tool was found.

Entity Model

erDiagram CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "brands" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies" CatalogBrand { int Id PK string Brand } CatalogType { int Id PK string Type } CatalogItem { int Id PK string Name string Description decimal Price string PictureFileName int CatalogTypeId FK int CatalogBrandId FK int AvailableStock int RestockThreshold int MaxStockThreshold bool OnReorder }

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are defined under src/eShopModernizedMVC/Models/. CatalogDBContext maps them to the Catalog, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType tables. The model requires item name, constrains price and stock-related values, and relates each item to one brand and one type. Picture URI and temporary-image values are not persisted.

The project has no separate repository interfaces; ICatalogService is the application-facing data service abstraction.

Caching Strategy

No active catalog cache was identified. MVC output caching is configured with a zero duration and NoStore=true; Redis session configuration is commented out in Web.config. Mock-data mode is an in-memory development implementation, not a production cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The application has one relational database and one catalog bounded context; no cross-service database sharing or CQRS flow was identified. Catalog operations go through ICatalogService and its Entity Framework-backed implementation. Image content is stored separately through the image service when Azure storage is enabled. No other service consumes catalog data through a remote API.
